To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Obesity is accompanied by changes in the endocannabinoid levels and expression in peripheral tissues and organs.

the levels of endogenous endocannabinoids (anandamide and 2-archidonoylglyceride), but not of N-acylethanolamines (oleoylethanoamine and palmitoylethanoamide) are altered in peripheral tissues of the obese Zucker rats.
the levels of the endocannabinoids AEA, 2- AG and PEA are altered in peripheral tissues of Zucker obese rats, whereas the levels of OEA are unchanged.

the study of the endocannabinoidome in obese Zucker rats, and it represents the first step in a wider investigation of the endocannabi-noidome, aimed at understanding its role in the onset of obesity and related disorders.

the study of the "endomembrane" in the Zucker rat model, a widely used model of obesity and type II diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the Zucker obese rat model, the endocannabinoid levels in peripheral tissues and organs are altered, with the most evident differences in the BAT and the small and large intestinal tissues.
the ECS is altered in the obese Zucker rat model and that the alterations are tissue-specific and may be associated with the metabolic phenotype.
obesity is associated with changes in the endocannabinoidome, which are tissue-specific and may represent a key mechanism underlying the pathophysiology of metabolic disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obese Zucker rats show a reduced anandamide tone in BAT and small intestine, a reduced 2-AG tone in small and large intestine and a reduced OEA tone in BAT.
the endocannabinoid tone is altered in obese Zucker rats in a way that could be beneficial for the obese phenotype.

the ECS is differentially altered during obesity in different tissues, and that the changes of ECS components and activity are accompanied by differential alterations in the gene expression related to their metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECS is altered in obese Zucker rats and that this is accompanied by differential alterations in the levels and/or activity of the main endocannabinoids.
the levels of endogenous cannabinoids are different in obese rats and this is accompanied by differential changes of the genes regulating the ECS tone.
the levels of endogenous cannabinoids in peripheral tissues and their regulation are altered during obesity.
